approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a score-ranked survivor population. It samples preferred score quantiles, uses connected-fragment crossover and ordinary local mutation walks to fill a fresh surplus pool, then checks molecular validity, stable canonical identity and duplicates. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. An active Gaussian process uses count-Morgan features and every real accepted score from the current task; correlated posterior draws allocate the announced evaluation batch. Accepted offspring enter the full model archive and compete for the bounded greedy survivor population, so later breeding can build on earlier generated molecules.
approach.novelty: Freeze only the breeder to its ordinary initial usable, score-ranked cohort. Every later graph proposal still uses the inherited parent-draw and graph-edit rules, and the posterior continues learning from all real accepted offspring. Updated survivors remain available for incumbent tracking and reporting but cannot become breeding parents. Earlier controls removed crossover, ordinary continuation or predictive allocation; this probe preserves those mechanisms and cuts the accepted-offspring-to-breeder feedback path. It measures that recursive feedback within the current optimizer, while leaving the broader whole-optimizer question open.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting uncertainty in n-62daf219c70a is whether its strong recursive dependence on accepted offspring adds useful search beyond graph generation from initial scored parents plus active accepted-label posterior learning. The actual Parent summary.json and run.log pairs are complete, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. A fresh read-only reconstruction of all fifteen task logs verifies 110295 actual parent draws, of which 105073 use generated accepted offspring, from 2401 distinct reused offspring. Such parents occur in 72737 of 75961 breeding attempts; first reuse occurs in batch two in every task/seed session. Generated offspring are in the live score-quantile support in all 420 post-initial batches. Of 4350 accepted offspring, 4176 have scored-parent ancestry depth at least two; maximum depth ranges from 13 to 23 across sessions. The ordinary initial cohort contains ten usable molecules per session, but its unexcluded quantile support contains only five, so freezing this cohort can materially restrict the evolving search front. These counts demonstrate reuse, not its causal score value. The Parent also makes 435 accepted-only GP fits with 60900 generated-record occurrences among 65250 training rows, exposing the independent learning path this control must retain. n-4fa9546e559e originally demonstrated recursive breeding activation on only one unpaired screening seed, not a foundation contribution. Current component removals n-01b48dd09404, n-767d2ce08797 and n-dbee08307e86 lose mean 0.12438789088524467, 0.054937284705486644 and 0.02686763734135833 respectively but preserve improving task-seed exceptions; their useful components are not an additive proof of the whole loop. Under an older binary Parent, n-2bb53b5f7b44 reuses 14 relocation products in 979 parent selections across 972 later attempts, yet loses panel mean 0.0015770554771336414 and has mixed seed changes. Extensive or locally useful ancestry therefore does not by itself establish endpoint benefit.
hypothesis: Sever recursive accepted-offspring breeding feedback by fixing every breeding-parent draw and breeding-cohort availability check to an immutable copy of the ordinary initial usable score-ranked population, while preserving active posterior learning from all real accepted observations and the live survivor updates used for tracking and reporting.

finding_summary.headline: Recursive breeding feedback contributes: fixing initial parents lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.260206.
finding_summary.insights:
These complete, exposed results establish positive conditional contribution of recursive offspring-to-breeder feedback within the current optimizer, even while accepted-label posterior learning remains active. The initial cohort contains ten molecules, but only five have positive support under the inherited unexcluded quantile law. Fixing that breeder holds membership, ordering and cohort size together; this experiment cannot apportion their effects or isolate the survivor rule. It also leaves the broader whole-foundation question open. Separate component removals and shared-Parent siblings cannot be added into a joint value estimate.

The local success counts illustrate why ancestry and endpoint quality must be kept separate. Beating an initial molecule becomes more common, and prediction errors are smaller on the changed evaluated distribution, yet the search makes fewer incumbent gains and ends lower. Every Child endpoint still exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds useful available amines, ring closures and scaffold rearrangements alongside recurring initial amide, nitrile/carbonyl and dione organizations. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more familiar local chemistry than the higher-scoring Parent leaders. The deficit therefore does not establish an absence of chemical novelty, require reactive motifs, or identify a chemical mediator. Scored ancestry depth one also allows unscored multistep edits and crossover finishing.

The fixed neighborhoods remained productive enough to fill all full pools under inherited bounds, although they required more attempts. No rescue from live survivors was used. Exhaustion and recovery semantics passed source and synthetic checks but were not naturally exercised. Three matched Search seeds support this descriptive conditional result; they do not establish universal reliability or value for unobserved descendants.
finding_summary.results:
Every one of 122,044 Child parent draws came from the unchanged initial cohort; no accepted offspring became a breeding parent. The Parent used accepted offspring in 105,073 of 110,295 draws. All fifteen task/seed sessions matched through their first complete batch, then diverged at the first parent, pool member and evaluated molecule of batch two. Generated offspring still entered the live survivors and the full score archive. All 435 accepted-label posterior fits and original sampled-maximum allocations remained active. All pools filled, all three seeds completed, and no natural fallback or exhaustion occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.335464, a paired change of -0.260206 against the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.306557, -0.273839 and -0.200221. Every one of fifteen task-seed endpoints and all five task means declined. Population deviation across seed macros rose from 0.026593 to 0.047795. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 2,007 against the easier fixed initial comparators, while incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 84. Generation also encountered more duplicate proposals: 14,385 versus 6,358.

molecular.headline: Conventional amides and aromatic frameworks recur; useful free amines emerge, but alternative useful arrangements remain uneven
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-4d4b5eafa8b3 and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch and no uncovered objective. Each task contributes 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations, with complete matched Parent trajectories and identical fixed initial molecule/score records. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, while every matched Parent endpoint remains higher. This is not an absence of chemical improvement over the initial observations. The evaluated Child molecules repeatedly retain recognizable indole carboxamide, polyaryl nitrile/carbonyl, pyrrolidine acid/amide and nitrogen-dione motifs. Useful scaffold rearrangements and available amines also occur, and many leaders avoid the Parent leaders' reactive N-halogen or cyclic-cumulene environments. Child ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9517, 0.9552, 0.9034, 0.9736 and 0.8391 in fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9437, 0.9506, 0.8471, 0.9678 and 0.731. These are incidences of text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, despite available amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres. The digest reports 639, 782, 783, 702 and 765 distinct identities across the respective Child panels. A separate check confirms 300 distinct accepted identities within every task/seed, so cross-seed recurrence is not within-run duplicate evaluation or a failure of the budget ledger. Diversity is moderate across the recognizable molecular families and narrower among repeated leading series. The moderate drug-likeness judgement reflects familiar amide, ether, carbonyl and amine chemistry in the leaders, not strong biological performance or proved synthesis. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable for parts of the evaluated stream because of N-O/N-N ring connections, unusual sulfur or halogen environments, enlarged joined frameworks and unspecified stereochemistry. The strongest Child leaders do not universally have those liabilities; conventional-looking molecules can still have substantially lower supplied scores than questionable Parent molecules. Read-only RDKit perception supports size and functional-group descriptions; no new objective, feasibility or affinity scores were calculated. The initial observations, the frozen usable breeding cohort, and the subset actually selected as scored parents are distinct. For each retained task/seed leader, the audit joins its pool, emission and accepted-observation records and the recorded scored starting parents. The registered condition fixes initial-cohort breeding sources while retaining real accepted-label posterior allocation and live survivor updates. Source excerpts were read to interpret those records; this report does not decide activation or isolation. An unscored mutation intermediate or crossover product is not a newly scored breeding parent. A product can differ substantially from its initial sources through crossover and successive graph edits; fixed scored ancestry does not imply one atom edit or conservation of an initial scaffold. A pool member, an emitted offspring, an accepted scored molecule, a live survivor and the retained best endpoint are also different observations. The digest and chemical frequencies describe accepted trajectories, not every pool member or rejected graph. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 evaluations, not the best molecule of every seed. No absence from the evaluated leaders is promoted into absence from the full pool, and unselected alternatives receive no invented labels. The original n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry report and its carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh evidence index. Each transferable gap retains its original provenance and current conditions. Only digest/trusted-trajectory Child SMILES are quoted; Parent-only molecules are described by published task/seed/evaluation. Audits under .slots/r0018-02-ablation-L01/molecular/ include trajectory_audit.json, inspected_records.json, leader_provenance.json with log/source hashes, identity_scope_check.json and history_molecular_sources.json. No source or trajectory path was missing. Chemical resemblance and leader ancestry do not isolate the effect of a particular edit, membership/rank/size change or survival rule, identify mediation, or establish the contribution of the entire graph-evolution foundation. The retained predictive learning channel and live survivors prevent interpreting this condition as deletion of all feedback or the full optimizer.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules in all Child seeds are compact N-H indole carboxanilides with ordinary aryl fluorine, methoxy, methyl and sometimes methylthio substituents. They retain the recognizable aromatic/amide organization of the initial trimethoxyindole anilide, while replacing or relocating peripheral methoxy groups. A separate useful family is a phenyl/heteroaryl pyrazoline bearing a thioacyl group; the output is therefore not restricted to the indole skeleton. Mean Child SMILES length is 40.3, with a maximum of 63 and halogen-string incidence 0.754. These leading indole amides have relatively conventional bonds and no N-halogen or peroxide motif. The Parent leaders instead include an amino-substituted cumulene on N-chloro indole (seed 0, evaluation 289), an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide with N-F (seed 1, 293), and an N-chloro indole vicinal diketone (seed 2, 294). The Child leaders look chemically more familiar locally, while all matched retained scores are lower. That contrast does not establish that the Parent liabilities are required.
liabilities: The leading indole amides have conventional local bonding; their limitations concern repetitive leading chemistry and unverified overall properties rather than a universal reactive-bond defect.
Thioacyl, methylthio and thiolmethyl variants require environment-specific stability assessment, while enlarged acetal-bearing or ring-opened relatives introduce additional conformational complexity.
Conventional small rings and tiny stable molecules can still score zero when the combined molecular context is absent; that is a score observation, not chemical invalidity.
missing_features: The leading set does not consistently explore distinct compact arrangements beyond variants of the initial indole amide; the useful pyrazoline family is a real exception, so there is no global inability to change scaffold.

Conventional alternative frameworks expressing the stronger Parent score associations are not demonstrated at comparable scores, but the observed ordering does not identify an exact absent pharmacophore or justify requiring N-halogen bonds.
Stereochemical identity is unresolved in the saturated pyrazoline and more complex relatives, although the flat leading indole amides themselves do not require a stereocentre assignment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. A dimethoxy/methyl relative scores 0.36371550417720466, while a methoxy/dimethyl leader reaches 0.38277504802042894; another positional isomer shares 0.38277504802042894. The methylthio-containing seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.38236359684532834 and 0.38236359684532834. The pyrazoline thioacyl example reaches 0.37402294333585284, compared with 0.1501184006136499 for the related initial pyrazoline/thioamide framework. Inserting a methylene between indole and its amide gives 0.22116953418646673, a large acetal-bearing aryl substituent gives 4.874557967239721e-07, and isolated oxetane scores 0.0. These observations favor a compact connected aromatic/polar arrangement and particular peripheral composition; they do not support merely adding rings or heteroatoms. Structurally nearby evaluated examples are comparisons, not a demonstrated scored ancestor chain. Matched retained best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.38277504802042894 / 0.39405142067435733; seed 1: 0.38236359684532834 / 0.47411701813450596; seed 2: 0.38236359684532834 / 0.438972502037081. These supplied endpoints do not identify a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader (evaluation 15) is a methoxy/methyl-substituted benzofused N/O carbonyl heterocycle linked to a fluorinated biaryl nitrile. Seed 0 instead reaches an extended chromenone-like polyaryl nitrile bearing an additional fused diaza-aromatic unit. Seed 2 joins a related aryl/pyridyl nitrile carbonyl system to an aryl-substituted fused nitrogen dione. These are medium-sized to extended aromatic assemblies with recognizable nitrile, ether and carbonyl groups. Mean Child SMILES length is 61.4, maximum 130, and halogen-string incidence 0.3874. The leaders avoid the O-F, peroxide and N=S chemistry in the Parent seed-0 and seed-2 leaders, but some Child examples are much larger and more aryl-rich. Leader receipts link the current examples to initial aryl nitrile/carbonyl, dione or quinoline-containing sources; the seed-1 leader records successive graph edits, so a fixed scored source is not a one-edit neighbourhood. The Parent compact linked carbonyl-thione leader (seed 0, evaluation 281) and other Parent leaders (seeds 1 and 2, evaluation 296) remain higher-scoring. Their reactive local groups do not make them validated chemical targets.
liabilities: Extended polyaryl surfaces and numerous linked ring systems create size, conformation and synthetic-route concerns even when their local bonds are conventional.
Some lower-scoring evaluated recombinations introduce unusual carbonyl/sulfone connections; similar-looking aromatic richness does not preserve the useful functional arrangement automatically.

The largest joined molecules add considerable connectivity without consistently exceeding the smaller leaders. A molecular graph and a score do not establish accessibility or useful physical properties.
missing_features: The Child evaluated leaders do not recover the compact Parent seed-0 heterocyclic organization. This is a missing high-scoring arrangement in the evaluated set, not proof that similar chemistry is absent from the generated pool.

Reliable compact alternatives to the extended polyaryl combinations are not established throughout the leading set; the comparatively compact seed-1 leader shows that less molecular bulk can already be useful.
No exact missing target motif follows from these scalar scores, and the useful Child nitriles and ordinary ethers argue against a requirement for the Parent peroxide or O-F groups.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl nitrile/chromenone and aryl fused dione score 0.5418375031378128 and 0.548381482770623. The Child seed-1 N/O heterocycle reaches 0.5883938481052798, while the larger seed-0 and seed-2 linked systems reach 0.5771747634966925 and 0.5804597701149425. A quinoline-ether/dione assembly scores 0.5800466171870208 and a still larger late joined system 0.5546463721675441. Increased aryl size alone therefore does not consistently improve reward. The small aryl sulfone scores 0.2530774641695243 and a sulfone-linked dione derivative 0.3187137024897936, below the 0.5 value of a small alkynol. The common 0.5 value for simple fragments is not the observed global floor in this panel. The gradient associates useful reward with particular linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements, not rings or sulfur in isolation. Matched retained best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.5771747634966925 / 0.8561477222467935; seed 1: 0.5883938481052798 / 0.6248206599713055; seed 2: 0.5804597701149425 / 0.6178024026512013. These supplied endpoints do not identify a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: Much of the evaluated Child material retains the initial fluoromethoxy-biaryl carboxylic-acid/amide/pyrrolidine framework and its aryl-sulfonyl region. The seed-0 leader (evaluation 294) adds an aryl methyl and places a methylene between pyrrolidine nitrogen and the aryl sulfone, leaving an available tertiary amine. The seed-1 leader instead has an expanded partially unsaturated nitrogen ring and an enamine-like linkage while retaining the bulky acid/sulfonamide context. The strongest Child example, seed 2 evaluation 121, is smaller: an aryl carboxylic acid linked through a secondary amine/methylene to N-methylpyrrolidine, with the aryl sulfone and amide carbonyl absent. Mean Child SMILES length is 67.4, maximum 135, and halogen-string incidence 0.8851. The bulky acid/amide/sulfone assemblies coexist with that more recognizable available-amine derivative. The Parent leaders are a flexible aryl tertiary amine (seed 0, evaluation 284), an aminoalkyl pyrrolidine/aryl ether (seed 1, 261), and a pyrrolidine/fused thioether/biaryl framework (seed 2, 241). The Child therefore does produce useful available amines, but does not consistently reach the Parent's stronger aryl-amine arrangements across evaluated seeds.
liabilities: Several leading or late evaluated examples remain bulky and multifunctional, with large halogenated aryl surfaces plus acid, amide and sulfone regions; their combined physical properties and synthesis are untested.
Some evaluated variants introduce N-Cl or an unusual S=C/S=O environment. These are not necessary features of the strongest Child amine and should not be generalized to all leaders.
Unassigned stereochemistry and different amine/amide/sulfonamide environments prevent treating all nitrogen-containing variants as equivalent pharmacological objects.
missing_features: Available aliphatic amines in a useful aryl environment are not consistently realized across the evaluated seed leaders, despite a clear successful example. Basic amines are not absent from the chemistry or from the initial observations.

The output does not consistently disentangle useful aryl/amine relationships from bulky acid/amide/sulfone or acetal material. The acid-retaining leader is an explicit limit on any recommendation to remove all acidic groups.
Stereochemistry of benzylic and cyclic-amine centres is unspecified. Protonation is a separate unresolved question; neutral SMILES do not imply a lack of basicity.

The N-methylpyrrolidine amide relative scores 0.11854231818713744 and the corresponding amine/methylene-linked example 0.6832960028134325. The latter retains the carboxylic acid, so the observations do not establish that removing acid is necessary. These molecules were evaluated at different times and are not a scored ancestor/descendant sequence: the leader receipt records crossover between initial sources followed by deletion. The sulfonylmethyl-linked seed-0 tertiary amine reaches 0.2862743315888403, while a small N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine scores 0.00021169315013374197. The visible positive association concerns nitrogen availability in a particular aryl arrangement, together with selective simplification, rather than atom count or deletion of every polar group. Matched retained best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.2862743315888403 / 0.9999989177995104; seed 1: 0.08478148896388923 / 0.9969753164881906; seed 2: 0.6832960028134325 / 0.9999934235240012. These supplied endpoints do not identify a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: The Child seed-1 and seed-2 leaders retain a quinoline-methyl ether/phenyl/piperidine-carbonyl organization recognizable in an initial molecule, with new ring closures around the nitrogen/carbonyl region. Seed 1 contains an N-N ring connection with N-hydroxy substitution; seed 2 instead closes through an N-O-N segment. Seed 0 retains a different diaryl partially saturated nitrogen-dione system with an ethyl ester, phenol and aryl chlorine. These are medium-sized molecules combining aromatic surfaces, saturated amines and multiple carbonyls. Mean Child SMILES length is 56.5, maximum 130, and halogen-string incidence 0.1736. The leader receipts record initial carbonyl frameworks as scored sources, including ring-closure products of the initial hydroxamate-containing molecule. The Parent also has bridged nitrogen-carbonyl chemistry, but its leaders (seed 0 evaluation 293; seeds 1 and 2 evaluations 278 and 261) reorganize the aryl and carbonyl regions into different fused/bridged systems with higher supplied scores. The Child does not lack nitrogen diones, aromatic rings or ring-forming capability; its leading arrangements remain different.
liabilities: The new ring-closing heteroatom environments need specific stability and synthetic-route assessment; an RDKit-valid closure does not demonstrate that the molecule is readily accessible.
Occasional O-Br or peroxide-containing derivatives coexist with conventional dione leaders. Those local liabilities are not the common source of all Child score limitations.
The fused and saturated ring centres remain stereochemically unspecified; the score gains from individual closures do not validate their configurational or conformational identity.
missing_features: The evaluated set does not consistently reach an alternative arrangement of the already-present aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl regions at the Parent score range; an exact absent target motif cannot be read from the scalar values.
Chemical and geometric identity of the new N-N/N-hydroxy and N-O-N ring connections is unresolved, together with stereochemistry of saturated ring junctions.
Plausible alternatives within leading series remain limited, while the distinct non-N-O/N-N dione family prevents treating those unusual closures as universal requirements.

The Child N-N/N-hydroxy and N-O-N ring-closure leaders reach 0.188720886308341 and 0.1923146091852909. The seed-0 aryl-chlorinated dione reaches 0.18621671123355962; its nonchlorinated counterpart scores 0.18288232814010746. The useful association is combined aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl organization. Neither reactive heteroatom substitution nor more rings is independently established as necessary. These supplied endpoints do not identify a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: The Child seed-0 and seed-2 leaders are small N-alkyl trimethoxyindole carboxamides; seed 2 also has an indole methyl substituent. The seed-1 leader is a hydroxy/methyl azaaryl group linked to an aryl-substituted fused nitrogen dione. These leading molecules are unfluorinated and use conventional amide or dione chemistry. A fluoromethoxy indole amide and a smaller azaindole ketone are nearby useful alternatives, so fluorine is possible but not a feature of every Child leader. Mean Child SMILES length is 39.1, maximum 107; aromatic-string incidence is 0.731 and halogen-string incidence 0.3333. The rest of the evaluated stream includes isolated fragments, oxygen-rich acetal material and very large joined aryl/carbonyl assemblies. The Parent leaders instead are compact fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles in seeds 0 and 1 (evaluations 276 and 290) and a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring joined to a cyclic cumulene in seed 2 (273). The Child leaders avoid those N-F/cyclic-cumulene liabilities but do not reach comparable supplied scores. Their conventional local bonding is a chemical counterexample to equating higher benchmark score with greater plausibility.
liabilities: The leading simple amides are recognizable synthetic targets; their modest scores are not evidence of chemical invalidity. No universal reactive-bond defect is present in those leaders.

Large joined structures and oxygen-rich acetal frameworks add substantial complexity while scoring extremely poorly in this record. Their poor values do not reveal which individual region is responsible.
Some evaluated proposals still introduce peroxide or N-Cl chemistry, but these do not define the leading Child family and cannot be assigned as mediators of the overall paired loss.
missing_features: The evaluated leaders do not demonstrate the compact condensed imino/carbonyl and fluorinated substituent arrangements seen in the higher-scoring Parent series. This is an observed leading-family difference, not a requirement for N-F or cyclic cumulenes and not a claim about every unselected pool molecule.

Useful independent polar arrangements beyond close indole-amide and azaaryl-dione variants remain unevenly represented. The available azaindole ketone and successful unfluorinated leaders rule out a simple absence of heterocycles or fluorine-only explanation.

Stereochemical identity is unresolved in the more complex saturated/acetal material, although the flat leading indole and azaaryl dione molecules do not themselves require tetrahedral stereocentre assignments.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The general chemistry concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. It is assessed here in n-4d4b5eafa8b3 versus that published Parent on complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. The current condition fixes initial usable scored breeding sources while retaining real accepted-label posterior allocation, graph intermediates and live survivor updates. Evidence concerns accepted evaluated molecules and their leaders; it is not a census of unselected pool chemistry, a total-foundation deletion test or additional historical replication. Leading output repeatedly retains indole carboxamides, aryl nitrile/carbonyl systems, pyrrolidine acid/amide material and nitrogen diones. Identical or closely related evaluated molecules recur across seeds, while the stronger Parent leading arrangements are often absent from the corresponding Child leaders. Counterexamples include a useful pyrazoline thioacyl family, linked heteroaromatic recombinations, new carbonyl-ring closures and a substantially improved available-amine derivative. Every current retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, so the finding is limited useful coverage rather than absence of molecular novelty or useful search.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently provide independent useful arrangements beyond recurring initial functional-group and scaffold combinations in evaluated output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically coherent alternatives that reorganize learned useful relationships under the legal task-local source and feedback rules, and assess their actual evaluated descendants. Do not equate new strings or one-edit distances with meaningful scaffold coverage. These observations cannot prescribe a benchmark-specific scaffold, show that missing chemistry was unavailable in the pool, or attribute an endpoint effect separately to membership, rank, cohort size, survival or the entire optimizer.

Small N-alkyl indole amides can substantially exceed their larger aryl-amide initial source, and an available-amine derivative improves while retaining a carboxylic acid. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
